properties.name: reflow2 conforms to the MCP specification revision it serves (2026-07-28 today), including everything reflow2 builds by hand rather than through the MCP library
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-09-28: "some other standards that we should consider: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28 (though I believe rust-sdk v3 package does automatically adhere to this standard)." Kept as intent the same day.

reflow2 conforms to the MCP specification revision it declares, currently 2026-07-28, on every surface it serves: stdio, --shared, --http, the registry server, the degraded and latent surfaces, and the --remote client.

WHY "AUTOMATICALLY" IS ONLY PART OF IT: rmcp (3.4.0 in the lock file) builds most messages, and what it builds follows the spec it implements. Whatever reflow2 builds by hand does not. MEASURED 2026-09-26 (fact:root-cause-the-latent-tool-list-omits-the-cache-fields-the-2026-07-28-spec-requires-2026-09-26): the latent surface's hand-built tool list omitted two fields the 2026-07-28 revision requires, and Claude Code rejected it. So conformance is checked on what reflow2 serves, not assumed from the library. Hand-built replies, the stateless-session rules (req:seat-identity-survives-stateless-mcp), and the authorization profile (req:every-oauth-role-reflow2-plays-meets-oauth-2-1-at-a-minimum) are all included.

A NEW REVISION is adopted deliberately: read it, list what changed, check what reflow2 serves against it, and record the result. It is never inherited silently by a dependency bump. How revisions are watched is req:the-hub-tracks-the-standards-reflow2-and-flo2-follow-and-reviews-each-new-revision in the hub's design.
